stories.title: Caleb Wilson's hand injuries not connected as Bulls rookie deals with 'bad luck'
stories.summary: Caleb Wilson has sustained three hand-related injuries in the past year, but the Chicago Bulls rookie said doctors told him they're not connected and that it's a case of "bad luck," he told reporters before his team's game against the Washington Wizards.
stories.detailText: CHICAGO -- Caleb Wilson has sustained three hand-related injuries in the past year, but the Chicago Bulls rookie said doctors told him the injuries aren't connected. "No, it's just bad luck," Wilson said before Friday's game against the Washington Wizards . "I'm pretty healthy. I do what I'm supposed to do. I drink my milk. So sometimes you just have a bad go at things." Wilson fractured his right hand during a game on Nov. 12 when he tried to knock the ball out of Victor Wembanyama's hands. He said he knew instantly -- because he heard the break. "I looked down at my hand, and it was bent the wrong way," he said. At North Carolina last season, Wilson missed the NCAA tournament after he needed surgery to repair a broken right thumb. He also missed six games during the regular season with a broken bone in his left hand. But Wilson said each injury was a freak accident. He wore a red-and-black sling on his right hand as he spoke to the media Friday and said he has been able to continue running and do some dribbling with his left hand. The Bulls begin a three-game homestand Friday and have nine of their next 10 games at home, so although Wilson might not travel with the team while he recovers, coach Tiago Splitter said he wants Wilson to learn from the bench while the team is at home. Chicago said Wilson will be reevaluated in three weeks following the injury; however, Wilson said he expects to return to the court soon. "I don't have an expectation of a timeline," Wilson said. "I just expect to be playing soon. I don't expect this to be season-ending or really make me miss a whole, whole bunch of games. But I expect to play whenever I feel good. And I feel like I'll feel good in a good amount of time." In his first 10 games after being drafted No. 4 in the 2026 draft, Wilson averaged 18.9 points, 6.2 rebounds and 1.9 assists on 42% shooting along with 1.8 steals and 0.9 blocks. After beginning the season 1-9, Chicago won three of its first four games with Wilson sidelined. "I feel like we were playing really well the last couple games before I got injured," Wilson said. "It's great that we're winning now. We had a great lead on the Spurs the game I went out. So I felt like this was due to happen."

stories.title: Jalen Rose admits interest in ‘Inside the NBA’ job after Charles Barkley’s ringing endorsement
stories.summary: Charles Barkley already has an idea of who he wants to replace him on "Inside the NBA."
stories.detailText: Charles Barkley already has an idea of who he wants to replace him on “Inside the NBA” — Jalen Rose. Rose, the former NBA player and longtime analyst, said Thursday that he would be interested in joining the award-winning studio show, with Barkley’s blessing, of course. “I love Charles, and yes, that would be something that I would be interested in,” Rose told Front Office Sports . “I love Charles, and yes, that would be something that I would be interested in.” Jalen Rose addressed the possibility of taking over for Charles Barkley on “Inside the NBA” once he retires. New episode drops at 11 p.m. ET on Samsung TV+ or check your local listings. pic.twitter.com/Vm4uiOrtB9 — Front Office Sports Tonight (@FOSTonight) November 20, 2026 Rose, 53, also expressed appreciation for the opportunities he has received to work alongside Barkley and the rest of the show’s cast, as the show opens up to other NBA standouts, like Rose and Draymond Green. “I appreciate my opportunities the last couple of years to not only contribute to Inside the NBA, but work with TNT on college basketball with Adam Lefkoe, Jamal Mashburn and Bruce Pearl,” Rose said. “It’s been a lot of fun for me.” Rose’s comments came more than a month after Barkley publicly endorsed Rose as his ideal replacement while on “BetMGM Gameday Live.” Shaquille O’Neal, Ernie Johnson, Jalen Rose, Kenny Smith and Charles Barkley talk before the game between the New York Knicks and the Indiana Pacers during Game 6 of the 2025 Eastern Conference Finals on May 31, 2025 at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis, Indiana. NBAE via Getty Images “I think Draymond would do a good job,” Barkley said in early October. “I like Draymond, but Jalen Rose is fantastic. He’s substituted for us sometimes, Jalen Rose is unbelievable, Vince Carter is unbelievable… but Jalen Rose to me, would be the perfect guy because he’s done the most with us.” Rose, who spent 16 years at ESPN before being a victim of the network’s 2023 layoffs , occasionally filled in on “Inside the NBA” and other basketball programming on TNT, the show’s broadcast home until 2026. He was greatly appreciative of Barkley’s endorsement. Jalen Rose attends the 16th Annual Jalen Rose Leadership Academy Celebrity Golf Classic Kick-Off Pairings Party in Detroit, Michigan, on July 26, 2026. Getty Images for Operation Gradu “The one thing I learned about this business is everything isn’t transactional,” Rose said. “If Charles Barkley is going to say into a microphone that you’re the person he feels should replace him, you can’t write a check for that, even if it never happens. Basically, what [Barkley is saying] is, ‘I’m running one lane in one race, and I’m considered the GOAT to a lot of people, but there’s somebody else that I feel like, you know what? “Y’all should put some respect on his name.’”

stories.title: Things look bleak for Warriors, but they can survive this
stories.summary: The bad news? The Warriors are in free fall, losing five games in a row, including their last four by 20 or more points. The good news? They can survive...
stories.detailText: The bad news? The Warriors are in free fall, losing five games in a row, including their last four by 20 or more points . The good news? They can survive this. Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry, right, confers with head coach Steve Kerr during an NBA game in Denver, Monday, Oct. 26, 2026. AP Photo/David Zalubowski Of the 15 Western Conference teams, only 11 are going to have a real shot at securing the 10 playoff spots unless something drastically changes. In other words, the West cellar is so weak that even if the Warriors can’t arrest their precipitous slide without Steph Curry, they’ll have more than enough time to recover when he returns. So, while what’s happening to the Warriors is unfortunate, it’s far from catastrophic. Curry is expected to be sidelined close to a month after suffering a right oblique abdominal tear on Nov. 11. The 38-year-old had carried the Warriors to eight straight wins while playing some of the best basketball of his career , averaging 27.8 points (50% shooting from the field, 45.7% from beyond the arc), 3.7 rebounds and 3.9 assists per game. Before Curry sustained the injury, he and Yaxel Lendeborg were looking like one of the NBA’s best duos. Lendeborg, whom the Warriors drafted with the No. 11 overall pick in June, was having a Rookie of the Year campaign, averaging 21.6 points on 52.2% shooting. But with defenses collapsing on him without Curry, the rookie has wilted, averaging 13.7 points on 26.8% shooting over the last four games. But things are going to change. Help is coming. Not only is Curry going to be back in the lineup soon, but Jimmy Butler (torn right ACL) is expected to return midseason. The Warriors could still be really good. They could still have a deep playoff run. They could still be a contender. This has been a roller coaster for Warriors fans. Entering the season, it was questionable whether the Warriors would make the playoffs after they pretty much stood pat during the offseason. And after dropping their first three games, it seemed all but guaranteed that this was going to be a wasted season for Curry, a two-time MVP who carried the Warriors to four championships in eight years from 2015-2022. But then something unexpected happened. Lendeborg emerged as his sidekick. He sprinted past his expectations. He became a force. Yaxel Lendeborg, left, and Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr smile during a game against the Houston Rockets on Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026, in Houston. NBAE via Getty Images All of a sudden, Curry and Lendeborg were stomping on their competition, beating contenders such as the Lakers, Timberwolves and Nuggets over a stunning stretch that had pundits questioning whether the Warriors were championship contenders. But the short-handed Warriors were always one Curry injury away from disaster. And when their nightmare was realized, the Warriors went from being one of the league’s most fun teams to one of its biggest duds. Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr watches play during an NBA game against the San Antonio Spurs on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, in San Antonio. AP Photo/Darren Abate But this is a speed bump not a crevasse. Curry and Butler will return, and the Warriors will have more than enough runway to correct course. So the excitement the team was generating a little over a week ago? It’s just a Curry return away.

stories.title: Brandon Ingram expected to make season debut soon with Clippers
stories.summary: Brandon Ingram is set to make his season debut with the Los Angeles Clippers on Monday, Nov. 23 against the Houston Rockets, according to reports.
stories.detailText: Brandon Ingram is set to make his season debut with the Los Angeles Clippers on Monday, Nov. 23, according to ESPN’s Shams Charania . The Clippers will play the Houston Rockets at the Toyota Center in Houston on Monday. Ingram had been working his way back from right heel surgery he had in May. The two-time All-Star also had a partially torn Achilles tendon. Ingram was initially supposed to have a bone removed from his heel, but the doctors found the partially torn Achilles during that procedure. Earlier this month, Ingram told reporters that he was "pretty close" to returning and had been on the court a bit more. He also stated that he had not played any 5-on-5 during the summer but has since been "gaining that confidence." When did Brandon Ingram join Clippers? The Clippers acquired Ingram as one of the primary trade assets in the package sent over by the Toronto Raptors for Kawhi Leonard during the offseason. Ingram has remain close with the team since his arrival. He took some time to praise his teammates despite the Clippers’ slow start to the season. L.A. has a 4-10 record through the first 14 games. "I actually want to commend those guys because everybody is in new positions and asked to do more,” Ingram told reporters earlier this month. “So the guys are trying. They're playing really, really good defense.” The Clippers fell short in a 124-112 loss to the San Antonio Spurs , in what was a competitive game considering both teams are on opposite sides of the standings. What Brandon Ingram’s return means for Clippers Ingram return would be welcomed, especially on the offensive end of the floor. The All-Star led Toronto with 21.5 points and was third in rebounds (5.6) during the 2025-26 season. He started 77 games for the Raptors. “They're trying to figure it out on the offensive end,” Ingram told reporters. “When I come in, I want to play make, make it a little bit easier for guys to catch and shoot, and not have to make so many decisions. And be able to, when it gets down to it, be able to score." Ingram already had a level of familiarity with head coach Tyronn Lue and assistant coach Jeff Van Gundy from playing for Team USA during the 2023 FIBA World Cup. Clippers continue to get healthy The Clippers had several players injured to start the month, including Ingram, center Yanic Konan Niederhäuser and Max Strus. The trio was recalled on Nov. 2 and participated in a weekend assignment with the team’s G-League affiliate. Strus returned to the team after recovering from a partial tear to his right plantar fascia. Konan Niederhäuser made his season debut on Nov. 19 against the Clippers, after recovering from right Lisfranc surgery. Bradley Beal (right knee injury management) and Jordan Miller (left rotator cuff surgery) will remain the only Clippers without a timetable to return. stories.title: Dominick Barlow probable, Jaylen Brown out for Sixers vs. Bucks
stories.summary: Dominick Barlow appears set to make his season debut Saturday, but the Sixers still won't be at full strength against the Bucks.
stories.detailText: SALT LAKE CITY, UTAH - MARCH 21: Dominick Barlow #25 of the Philadelphia 76ers grimaces as he tries to run up the court after injuring his leg during the first half of a game against the Utah Jazz at the Delta Center on March 21, 2026 in Salt Lake City, Utah. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Chris Gardner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Reinforcements are finally on their way for the Sixers. Dominick Barlow appears ready to make his season debut, as he’s listed as probable for Saturday’s game against the Milwaukee Bucks. Tony Jones of The Athletic reported earlier Friday that Barlow was trending in that direction, and Barlow foreshadowed it on Instagram on Thursday as well. Still, for a Sixers team that’s been woefully short on frontcourt depth as of late, his return could not be coming at a better time. Even with Barlow back, the Sixers won’t be at full strength against Milwaukee. Adem Bona (cervical spine strain), Jaylen Brown (hamstring) and Dean Wade (hamstring) are all out, while Tyrese Maxey is listed as questionable with a right foot sprain. For the Bucks, Ousmane Dieng (left finger fracture) is their only notable player who’s out. Luckily for the Sixers, the Bucks only loosely resemble a professional basketball team this year as they begin to chart a course in the post-Giannis Antetokoumpo era. They’re an NBA-worst 1-15, and this will be their third game in four days. The 1 p.m. ET start likely won’t do their tired legs any favors. Since this will be Barlow’s first game back this season, the Sixers figure to ease him in slowly. It’d be surprising if he played more than 15-20 minutes at most. Still, it’ll bear watching how the Sixers deploy him. Will he stick strictly to the 4, or will he cut into Tacko Time and steal some minutes at backup center whenever Joel Embiid is off the floor? Barlow was a revelation for the Sixers last year, averaging 7.7 points and 4.8 rebounds in 23.8 minutes per game while shooting 53.9 percent from the field. They initially signed him to a two-way contact last offseason, but he played so well for them—he even started 59 games!—that they wound up spending a hefty chunk of their taxpayer mid-level exception to convert him to a standard contract after the trade deadline. Barlow’s three-point shooting might be the swing skill that determines his place in the Sixers’ rotation this year. He knocked down only 25.6 percent of his long-range attempts on low volume last season, which won’t cut it moving forward. Jabari Walker’s improvement from deep gives him the inside track to backup frontcourt minutes, but it’s worth seeing how a Walker-Barlow pairing fares defensively, particularly with regard to rim protection. The Sixers proved Wednesday that they’re capable of winning even with Brown, Wade and Maxey out. Regardless of whether Maxey returns, they should be able to take care of business against an overmatched Bucks team. But Barlow’s return adds some extra juice to an otherwise sleepy 1 p.m. ET start against a lottery-bound squad.

stories.title: Brandon Ingram expected to make season debut for Clippers on Monday vs. Rockets
stories.summary: Ingram has been sidelined since May after undergoing surgery to repair a partially torn Achilles, discovered while getting a bone spur removed from his heel.
stories.detailText: Brandon Ingram is expected to make his 2026-27 season debut for the Los Angeles Clippers on Monday against the Houston Rockets, according to ESPN's Shams Charania . Before opening training camp, the Clippers announced that Ingram had been diagnosed with a partially torn Achilles tendon in his right leg. The partial tear was discovered while the two-time All-Star underwent surgery to remove a bone spur from his right heel in May. That heel injury caused Ingram to miss Games 6 and 7 of the Toronto Raptors' first-round playoff defeat to the Cleveland Cavaliers. Ingram was traded by Toronto to the Clippers as part of a package including Gradey Dick, unprotected 2031 and 2033 first-round selections, a 2027 first-round swap and second-round picks in 2030 and 2033 in exchange for Kawhi Leonard. The deal was originally agreed upon in late June and expected to become official on July 6 when the NBA's moratorium on transactions ended. However, the trade was put on hold amid the NBA's investigation into the Clippers allegedly evading the league's salary cap while signing Leonard to a three-year, $103 million free-agent contract in July 2019. Kobe Sanders hyped up Brandon Ingram in the background of his interview at Clippers practice. Sanders: “Uh oh! Uh-oh! That means he's coming back soon?” Brandon Ingram then adds: “I'm coming back soon, for sure. I've been on the floor with the rest of the guys, doing some… pic.twitter.com/cGAR0qRyA3 — Tomer Azarly (@TomerAzarly) November 6, 2026 Both the Clippers and Raptors agreed that the trade wouldn't be completed until the league's probe was completed. The deal finally went through in mid-September, approximately two weeks before NBA teams opened their training camps. The Clippers knew about Ingram's Achilles tear — repaired in the same procedure that removed his bone spur — before agreeing to the trade, according to interim president of basketball operations Trent Redden. Redden told reporters that Ingram would require about six fewer months of rehab with a partial tear and expected he would play for the Clippers this season. Ingram averaged 21.5 points, 5.6 rebounds and 3.7 assists for the Raptors last season after being acquired from the New Orleans Pelicans in early 2025. Shortly after joining Toronto, he signed a three-year, $120 million contract extension . During his 10 NBA seasons, Ingram has averaged 19.8 points, 5.2 rebounds and 4.2 assists while shooting 37% on 3-pointers. He was the Los Angeles Lakers' 2016 first-round pick (No. 2 overall) out of Duke. Ingram played three seasons for the Lakers before being traded to New Orleans as part of a three-team deal that sent Anthony Davis to L.A . Without Ingram, the Clippers are off to a 4-10 start that currently has them as the third-worst team in the Western Conference . The team has also been without Bradley Beal (knee) and Jordan Miller (shoulder) during the opening weeks of the season.

stories.title: Brandon Ingram set to make Clippers season debut Monday against Rockets
stories.summary: Ingram has been out since May when heel surgery revealed a partially torn Achilles tendon.
stories.detailText: An NBA All-Star is coming OFF the injured list. That is a refreshing change of pace. Brandon Ingram will return to the Clippers on Monday night when they travel to face the Houston Rockets, a story broken by Clippers reporter Ohm Youngmisuk and ESPN’s Shams Charania . Brandon Ingram is on track to make his season debut in Houston on Monday night. Ingram returns after being sidelined following offseason heel surgery. The 2-time All-Star is looking forward to being more of a playmaking scorer for the Clippers. — Ohm Youngmisuk (@NotoriousOHM) November 20, 2026 Ingram has been out since May, when he underwent heel surgery, which revealed a partially torn Achilles tendon. This wasn't a full-blown rupture, his return to the court was going to be quicker, but it did cause him to miss training camp and the start of the season. Ingram had a bounce-back season in Toronto before his injury, averaging 21.5 points a game, shooting 38.2% from 3, grabbing 5.6 rebounds a night, and earning an All-Star selection. He was traded to the Clippers in September as part of the Kawhi Leonard deal. Ingram should be a floor-raiser for a Clippers offense that is 23rd in the NBA this season — Ingram is a bucket-getter. Paired with point guard Darius Garland and with solid role players around them in Derrick Jones Jr., Rui Hachimura, Brook Lopez and Kris Dunn. The Clippers also got center Yanic Konan Niederhauser back following foot surgery on Thursday. However, they remain without Bradley Beal (right knee injury management) and Jordan Miller (shoulder surgery), and there is no timeline for either of them to return.

stories.detailText: The Warriors have lost four straight games by 20 or more points, tying the longest such streak in franchise history which was set in 1997-98. After Steph Curry suffered a right oblique abdominal tear on Nov. 11, the Warriors have been flailing. Golden State Warriors’ Steph Curry plays during the NBA season opener against the Los Angeles Lakers in Los Angeles on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. London Entertainment They went from having won eight games in a row to dropping their last five contests, including a 38-point loss to the Spurs, a 21-point loss to the Pelicans, a 22-point loss to the Mavericks and a 28-point loss to the Grizzlies. It’s an unfortunate break for a Warriors team that was surging behind the 38-year-old Curry, who’s averaging 27.8 points (50% shooting from the field, 45.7% from beyond the arc), 3.7 rebounds and 3.9 assists per game. Curry is expected to be sidelined close to a month, per ESPN. The Warriors have been decimated by injuries this season. Jimmy Butler (torn right ACL) and Moses Moody (ruptured left patellar tendon) aren’t expected to return until midseason. Kristaps Porzingis stepped away from basketball indefinitely while dealing with an undisclosed health matter. And Brandon Williams has missed five straight games because of a mild left hamstring strain. Yaxel Lendeborg (1) of the Golden State Warriors handles the ball against the Memphis Grizzlies on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026, at FedExForum in Memphis, Tenn. NBAE via Getty Images Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, who turned heads at the top of the season with an impressive Rookie of the Year campaign , has greatly struggled without Curry. Over the Warriors’ last four games, he has averaged 13.7 points on 26.8% shooting. “It’s unfair to him to try to make him step into Steph’s role 13 games into his career,” Draymond Green told reporters Nov. 16. “So, depend on him like we need to, but lower what we’re expecting out of him to allow him to then just flow into it. I think, right now, we’re putting too much pressure on him, and it’s tough to deal with in game 13, 14.”

NBA Trade Lab: Dejounte Murray's trade request After formally requesting a trade last Friday , New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray has unsurprisingly been the player most involved in fan-created trades over the past seven days in our NBA Trade Lab . The Spurs traded Murray to the Hawks in 2022 for a massive haul: three first-round picks (including the Hawks' pick in the upcoming 2027 draft) and one first-round pick swap. At the time, Murray was viewed as a burgeoning young star with a strong impact on both sides of the ball. In Atlanta he expanded his offensive game, but his defensive impact, as measured by Net Points , fell off a cliff. In 2024, the Hawks sent him to the Pelicans in exchange for a package that included two first-round picks and Dyson Daniels , who went on to win Most Improved Player the following season . Now in 2026, it appears likely Murray will be on the move again, but his market is difficult to read. His impact metrics have been on the decline, and he's making over $30 million for the next two seasons after turning 30 years old. At the same time, he is undoubtedly a talented player who could certainly find a renaissance in the right situation. Let's look at some of the top fan-created trades to see what fans are thinking might be a realistic deal. Trade No. 1 Pelicans get: Jalen Green Phoenix Suns get: Dejounte Murray Green and Murray are similar in many ways, so a straight-up swap could make sense for both teams. Green is a talented scorer, but he lacks consistency and doesn't offer the ancillary skills to buoy him at a constant floor of positive impact. He is also only 24, the same age as Warriors Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg , so the Pelicans could see room to further develop him in their system. For the Suns, this would be a bet on their system. They have built a menacing defensive identity over the past two seasons and often punch above their weight through effort and hustle. Bringing Murray into this system could help to revive some of the defensive aspects of his game that have faded in recent years. Trade No. 2 Pelicans get: Four second-round picks Charlotte Hornets get: Murray In this unusual deal, the Pelicans get no players back. It is a valid trade because of the $40 million trade exception that the Hornets received in the LaMelo Ball trade. Four second-round picks may not sound like much, but in the process the Pelicans would also open up a $32 million trade exception of their own and would completely clear Murray's money off their books without receiving any undesirable contracts in return. The Hornets' offense has been really struggling this season, ranking last in Offensive Net Points per game, after losing their offensive engine in LaMelo Ball. Trading for Murray could inject some life into their offense, strengthening their guard play while they wait for Kon Knueppel to return from injury and Coby White to return to form after a slow start to his season. Trade No. 3 Pelicans get: De'Aaron Fox and Spurs 2029 first-round pick San Antonio Spurs get: Murray and Herb Jones The Pelicans here get a proven winner and veteran presence in Fox, who could help to mentor Jeremiah Fears and their other young players throughout their roster. They also receive a 2029 first-round pick to build their future draft capital. The Spurs are rolling right now and Fox has been playing great, so this would likely be a trade they consider only if things start to go downhill a bit and they decide they want to get off Fox's contract. San Antonio might be more interested in Murray than other teams, since he played some of his best basketball there. In this deal they also receive a very valuable player in Jones, whose defensive ability could slot perfectly into the Spurs' lineups and make the Victor Wembanyama -anchored defense even more impenetrable. -- Benjamin Tiemeyer Have any more ideas on what move the Pelicans should make involving Dejounte Murray? Brown confronted Tatum at a dinner in France about their future as teammates, per Charania. The former teammates will meet for the first time Tuesday night, as the Celtics head to Philadelphia (8 p.m. ET). NBA Trade Lab updates: How could the Lakers level up? The Los Angeles Lakers find themselves at the top of the Western Conference standings, with Luka Doncic playing like the best player in the world and leading the way in ESPN's Net Points Metric . Their projected win total from ESPN's Basketball Power Index that started the season at 45 has already increased to 53. They completely retooled their roster this past offseason after losing LeBron James in free agency to the Philadelphia 76ers , but their newly added pieces have jelled together quickly to leave fans around the league rethinking what the ceiling of this team could be. After sending out two first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps in the Walker Kessler sign-and-trade , the Lakers are very limited in remaining draft capital they could use to add another major piece through a trade. However, this hasn't stopped Lakers fans from diving into our NBA Trade Lab tool to cook up some mock trades in an attempt to find the Lakers another piece around the margins that could complete this roster for a deep playoff run. Trade No. 1: Lakers bring in Luka's former teammate Lakers get: P.J. Washington Dallas Mavericks get: Jarred Vanderbilt , Cameron Carr , and two second-round picks Washington is a versatile two-way wing who started alongside Doncic during the Mavericks' run to the finals in 2024. Washington played the best basketball of his career alongside Luka during their time together on the Mavs and would be a proven contributor to add to the Lakers' depth. Carr, the 24th overall pick in the 2026 draft, is a promising young player the Mavericks can plug in right away and develop around their young core. The two second-round picks would also be a welcome addition for Dallas, which currently doesn't have any second-round picks (outside of a top-55 protected Hawks' 2027 second-rounder). Trade No. 2: L.A. adds a big man Lakers get: Jalen Smith Chicago Bulls get: Jaden Hardy and two second-round picks Smith is a young intriguing stretch big, whose advanced metrics paint as a positive player even on a middling Bulls team. Despite averaging only 17 minutes a game in his career, Smith possesses a rare blend of rim defense, rebounding and 3-point shooting. This would be a buy-low opportunity for the Lakers to invest in the potential of Smith, letting him play off one of the best playmakers in the world in Luka Doncic . If the Bulls aren't as convinced about Smith's potential or are unsure of what kind of an extension they would give him this upcoming summer, they could decide to trade him before the deadline rather than lose him for nothing. Trade No. 3: Lakers get help on defense Lakers get: Derrick Jones Jr. LA Clippers get: Jaden Hardy and three second-round picks Jones is a talented defender who also started alongside Luka Doncic during the Mavericks' 2024 Finals run. He was an unsung hero throughout that 2024 playoff run as he held his own on defense against the likes of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Anthony Edwards . His thin frame combined with outlier athleticism allows him to navigate around screens and successfully shadow the shiftiest superstars in a way that few others in the league can. His addition to the Lakers as a reliable point-of-attack defender would be immensely helpful in slowing down an opposing star guard in a playoff series. The Clippers' future draft assets are severely depleted after the NBA stripped them of five future first-round picks for circumventing the salary cap. It makes sense for the Clippers to try to parlay any valuable veteran players on their current roster to start to recoup some future draft capital. Have any ideas on what move the Lakers should make? Build it in the NBA Trade Lab , then submit your trade to let fans vote on it from both sides. -- Ben Tiemeyer Nov. 9 NBA Trade Lab updates: The latest Sabonis deals As my colleague Ben Tiemeyer wrote earlier, Golden State Warriors center Kristaps Porzingis is the player most involved in fan-created trades in the new NBA Trade Lab. While Porzingis has the most interest, trading for Sacramento Kings center Domantas Sabonis could be the most impactful. The Kings sit in the bottom of the Western Conference standings and have prioritized building their roster with young players, notably lottery pick Darius Acuff Jr . They have gone from one of the oldest rosters in the NBA last season to a team with seven players 26 years old or younger this season. Sabonis was named All-NBA in 2024 and appeared in 82 games. However, last season he played the fewest games (19) in his career and had season ending knee surgery in February. Sabonis has two years and $94 million left on his contract ($45.5 and $48.6 million). Below are some of the top fan-created trades involving Sabonis, as scored by fans voting from the perspective of each team involved: Trade No. 1 Kings get: A top-4 protected first from a rebuilding Chicago is strong value for the Kings. Nic Claxton gives Sacramento a serviceable center with two years left on his contract. The negative is the $18 million owed to Patrick Williams in 2028-29. On "NBA Today," ESPN's Malika Andrews detailed Karl-Anthony Towns ' mindset toward contract negotiations with the defending champion New York Knicks . "Towns, from what I have been told, is willing -- similarly to what Jalen Brunson did [but the] numbers aren't the same -- to take a pay cut," Andrews said. "But the pay cut that the Knicks are asking him to take, he views as unreasonable." Towns, 30, is eligible to sign a four-year, $276 million extension through June 30. Embiid "full participant" in first Sixers' practice Joel Embiid was a "full participant all the way through" for the Philadelphia 76ers first practice of training camp, Sixers coach Nick Nurse said Tuesday. "He looked great," Nurse said of Embiid. "Very, very good news from the standpoint of where it's been the last couple years, last couple summers leading into today. ... It's great to see." After being named the league MVP in 2023, the 32-year-old center has missed 150 games over the last three seasons because of various injuries. He also sat out four of the Sixers' 11 playoff games in the spring because of appendicitis, right hip soreness and a right ankle sprain. The only Sixers player who did not participate in Tuesday's practice according to a team spokesperson was backup big man Adem Bona , who is dealing with a sprained left foot. Anfernee Simons , who signed a two-year, $12.3 million contract to join Philadelphia in July, said Embiid's presence in the gym was already notable leading up to the start of camp. "Everybody's been impressed around here about how he's come in and worked," Simons said. "Joel is going to be Joel. He's going to be a dominant player always. We just want to continue for him to be himself, as well, and I think everybody's going to be able to work around that." Despite the injuries, the 10-year veteran still averaged 26.9 points, 7.7 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 1.2 blocks per game last season. Embiid's inclusion only added to what several Sixers players described as an "exciting" opening day with LeBron James and Jaylen Brown completing their first official practice with the franchise. "With any team, we got to start somewhere, and then we got to get better and better, and just keep trying to reach our ceiling, right?" Nurse said. "That happens day-to-day. Can we get up tomorrow, like, 98% as excited as we did today? It's going to be hard to get as excited as we all were today, right? "But we need to come back, and we need to keep climbing that mountain. That's a daily process. I just want them to reach their potential. If they do, great things are going to happen." -- Dave McMenamin Hoop Collective: The 2026 NBA Media Day reaction special Brian Windhorst is joined by ESPN reporters from around the league to check in on Monday's Media Days. Tim MacMahon, Dave McMenamin, Vince Goodwill, Jamal Collier, Anthony Slater and Michael C. Wright all hop on the podcast to discuss the biggest storylines throughout the NBA ahead of training camp. "He said, 'I would like to stay in New York for the rest of my career.' And then he kind of ended it and because of the way the Knicks operated, it wasn't like you had space for a follow-up. "And then someone else, I think Ian Begley asked him, 'Are you OK with playing this out through the season or do you want to table contract talks?' and he basically said, 'Everybody's going to be a little uncomfortable around here.'" Latest episodes of the 'Hoop Collective' podcast Top NBA media day headlines LeBron says he envisioned joining Knicks as free agent | Philly stars ready to 'sacrifice' Clippers apologize to fans, vow to move past investigation | Ingram (Achilles) out Edwards happy to cede Wolves' PG duties to Ball Wizards, AD to wait until summer for extension talks Karl-Anthony Towns wants extension to stay with Knicks Jokic on his next Nuggets deal: 'I'm going to sign next year' Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path' Sept. 28 Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path' When LeBron James chose to leave the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency over the summer, he consulted his family on the decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers . But when it came to his son/teammate Bronny, much was apparently left unsaid . "We're men of very little words when it comes to talking about business and what we're going to do and how we feel about each other. So it wasn't really much [discussion] to be honest with you," Bronny James said Monday at Lakers media day. "He's got his own path and I got my own. He knows that I want to make a name for myself and I want to continue my career and keep growing as a player. And he knows that I want to focus on that. So he decided to do that." LeBron and Bronny have routinely been in unique situations in league history, whether it was opening night two years ago, when the father and son entered the game together, or last year in the playoffs, where they combined to deliver a 10-0 run during a victory over the Houston Rockets . Navigating a complex free agency in which the father leaves and the son stays is another one for the books. Tatum 'comfortable' leading new-look Celtics post-Brown trade Jayson Tatum 's one constant during his development into a star with the Boston Celtics was having Jaylen Brown as a teammate. That partnership ended this offseason when the Celtics' front office decided to trade Brown -- the 2024 NBA Finals MVP -- to the Philadelphia 76ers in what was largely a cost-cutting move that broke up the duo most responsible for leading Boston to the 2024 NBA championship. "The business of the NBA comes and plays a part at some point. And I've seen it in my almost 10 years in this league," Tatum said during Celtics media day on Monday . "For me it's more so being grateful for what we accomplished and what he means for this city and to this organization. Just the ups and downs in our career that we were able to grow and learn from and made us the players that we are today. So really just being thankful for those nine years." Suns owner Ishbia says mortgage company woes won't hurt team It's well-known at this point that billionaire Mat Ishbia's mortgage company has had a rough financial stretch. The owner of the Phoenix Suns said Monday that will have "zero" effect on his spending habits when it comes to basketball. In fact, the 46-year-old said he's working on purchasing 14% more of the team, bringing his total to roughly 80%. Ishbia's company -- United Wholesale Mortgage -- suffered a reported $450 million net loss in the second quarter this year, calling into question if the sizable dip would affect his basketball business. The outspoken Ishbia was adamant that nothing would change for the NBA franchise when it comes to spending on players or the fan experience. Williamson not where he wants to be New Orleans Pelicans forward Zion Williamson kept his answer brief when asked how he would summarize his first seven years as an NBA player. "I'm not where I want to be," said Williamson, whom the Pelicans drafted with the No. 1 pick out of Duke in 2019. "I'm not where I need to be." Butler indicates he is 'ahead' in his knee rehab Nearing the eight-month mark since his right ACL surgery , Jimmy Butler III is hesitant to put a specific target date on his eventual NBA return, but he did express optimism in advance of Golden State Warriors training camp. "I promise you I'm coming back, and it's going to be -- I think it's going to be, like, real eye-popping for everybody how I'm still going to be nice," Butler said. "Probably nicer, honestly." Butler has only recently advanced to running, and he will be limited to light on-court individual work when the team begins practice in Hawaii on Tuesday afternoon. It will be several weeks before Butler is expected to advance to a more rigorous stage of his rehab, and the team's lead medical decision-maker, Rick Celebrini, is known for his cautiousness in the later stages of the rehab process. A January or February return can be considered on the optimistic side for Butler, who turned 37 earlier this month. But Butler did say that the strengthening tests on the knee indicate he is ahead of schedule. "My numbers are staggering," Butler said. "They're off the charts. I'm ahead, so they say. So, I just know that all the work that I've been doing, whether it be at home, in L.A., in Europe, in South America, wherever the case may be, I've been doing all the right things. So, I am confident that whenever I come back, I'll be more than ready, I'll be more than healthy and I'll be a better all-around player than I was whenever I went down." -- Anthony Slater Pistons eye "better version" of Cunningham Detroit Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff has held many offseason conversations with All-NBA guard Cade Cunningham about seizing greatness and the necessary steps toward improving after last year's playoff run that stretched to Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semifinals. Bickerstaff has guaranteed "a better version" Cunningham this season, which could be a scary sight after he averaged 23.9 points, 9.9 assists, 5.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 33.9 minutes during 2025-26. But Cunningham also led the East in turnovers per game after finishing with the second most in 2024-25. "I don't have to challenge Cade, and that's why he is who he is," Bickerstaff said. "Because he's pulling. He's not being pushed." Cunningham showed up in a fresh pair of Nike S.T. Charge "Detroit Tough" sneakers in Pistons colors. He will also receive his own signature Nike shoe, which is expected to debut during the second half of the season. "I'm thankful to be in these shoes. I'm thankful to have the opportunity to represent my family in this way," Cunningham said. "Represent where I come from, but then to represent the city of Detroit. "In a city like this, it's a blessing. I'm thankful for it, I don't take it for granted and I'm trying to make the most out of it." -- Eric Woodyard Hornets waive former No. 8 pick Dillingham The Charlotte Hornets are waiving guard Rob Dillingham , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania . Dillingham was traded from the Chicago Bulls on Saturday for Buddy Hield and cash. The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the move. Dillingham, 21, appeared in 30 games for the Bulls last season, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists. SGA on chance at historic third straight MVP At Oklahoma City Thunder media day, guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander discussed the possibility of winning a third straight NBA MVP award and whether that's something he ponders going into this season. "No different than any other year: Try to be the best player I can be, try to implement the things I just worked on," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "The decision for MVP is literally 82 games away. I'm not going to win the award in the first week of the season. ... That kind of recipe for me in the past has kind of worked, and I've been fortunate to win two in a row. "We need to be laser focused on ourselves. We need to take the lessons from that [Western Conference finals] series, for sure, and we did. But it's certainly not something that we overcorrect for, because you end up chasing your shadow, and it prevents you from being your best as you move forward." ESPN's Summer Forecast gave Gilgeous-Alexander the fourth-best chance at the 2027 MVP, behind Victor Wembanyama , Nikola Jokic and Luka Doncic . No player has won three consecutive MVPs since Larry Bird in 1984, 1985 and 1986. -- Baxter Holmes Doncic talks LeBron exit, Lakers "championship" ceiling Speaking to ESPN's Brian Windhorst during Los Angeles Lakers media day, guard Luka Doncic detailed his reaction to LeBron James leaving for the Philadelphia 76ers this past summer and why he thinks a successful 2026-27 includes a Lakers run to the title: "It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him. ... We all know who LeBron James is." Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures" Simmons "didn't touch a ball for a year" During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season. "The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder." Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers . The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right." Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer. For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren will hold veto power on any trade this season and be an unrestricted free agent next summer. For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent is key. There are eight projected teams that have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract. "I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at media day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do." Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during Pistons media day. -- Bobby Marks Mitchell: LeBron to Cavs made sense "for a lot of reasons" At Cavaliers media day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense." "I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said. After being swept in the Eastern Conference finals by the eventual champion New York Knicks then missing out on James in free agency, Cleveland kept its core intact. The Cavs signed Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million maximum extension and re-signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million contract. Cleveland did make one major addition by acquiring Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets in a multiteam trade then signing the restricted free agent to a four-year, $88 million deal. Speaking for the first time since their extensions, Mitchell and Harden both said their approaches to their new deals -- Mitchell signing as soon as he was eligible with Harden opting out to give Cleveland more flexibility to make moves -- reflected a team-first mindset. "This is something that I want to do, and I want to win a championship," Harden said. "So, what does that look like? Making the team better, making the team whole to where we give ourselves a chance. By the way, you can have the best talented team, which I've been on before, and still not win. "We waited, waited, waited until the front office called me, made sure that we got everything that we can get, and then we signed. We got a long way to go, but I love the direction and steps that we're taking here as a unit from top to bottom." -- Daniel Oyefusi MacMahon: Thunder adjusting to roster changes The departures of three championship-winning teammates doesn't yet feel like reality for Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander , who kidded that he still expected Luguentz Dort , Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins to show up for Oklahoma City's team picture Monday afternoon. "It's the business of the NBA, right?" Gilgeous-Alexander said, referring to the series of financially motivated trades. "I don't think anybody has played with all 12 guys their whole career. It sucks a little bit. "My mind never even went to what we were going to be like on the court. It was more like the brotherhood." As fellow OKC guard Jalen Williams added, "It's the weirdest thing ever." -- Tim MacMahon Clippers announce Ingram has partially torn Achilles The LA Clippers announced they found a partially torn Achilles tendon in Brandon Ingram 's foot after his recent heel surgery. He will miss the start of the 2026-27 season. Jokic: "I'm gonna sign next year" Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic reiterated his commitment to the franchise at Monday's media day. "I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said. "If they want me." Curry said knee is ready to go for the season Golden State Warriors superstar guard Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday in offering positive updates on his injured knee. "Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with." Curry did acknowledge a "management element" but said there are currently no restrictions. Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise Members of the Denver Nuggets ' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer addressed the media on Monday and answered questions regarding Nikola Jokic 's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason. "We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns." LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title. "I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' media day. "One of the best places I've ever played. "I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it." James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20. No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr. 's contract. "I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that." The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason. Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant Portland Trail Blazers ' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday. "Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player. "I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent." Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant. Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton" Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season. "He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need. "Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks." Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season. Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey . "It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there." Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season. "I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said. Harper addresses role for coming season After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season. "Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in." First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team: "Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language." LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win. "Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything" Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings. "I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors." Haliburton: I am 100% healthy Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season. "I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year." Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team. In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors. Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room. "We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room." "I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control." And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done." Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday. Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft. Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday. Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said. Sept. 26 Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday. 2026 NBA offseason trade grades Sept. 25 What's next for Curry and the Warriors? Stephen Curry 's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings. The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer. By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million. For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer. Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski . The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks Grading the Curry deal: Why Warriors don't get an A Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury The Charlotte Hornets announced that Kon Knueppel will be out for at least the entire preseason because of a left hamstring injury. James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July. "[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump." Grizzlies waive Russell The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

stories.title: Game Preview: Suns chasing their longest winning streak of the season
stories.summary: The Suns have won two straight and can extend their longest winning streak of the season against an injury-riddled Utah team.
stories.detailText: PHOENIX, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 16: Miles Bridges #22 of the Phoenix Suns handles the ball against Svi Mykhailiuk #10 of the Utah Jazz during the second half of the preseason NBA game at Mortgage Matchup Center on October 16, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona.
