stories.title: Jets QB Geno Smith (ankle) cleared to start vs. Chargers
stories.summary: Jets quarterback Geno Smith made it through the practice week with no setbacks and was cleared to face the Chargers.
stories.detailText: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith , who said Wednesday that his plan is to play Sunday despite a balky left ankle, made it through the practice week with no setbacks and was cleared to face the Los Angeles Chargers . After two days of limited practice, Smith was a full participant Friday and has no injury designation on the final report. Before Friday's practice, coach Aaron Glenn said that Smith had looked "solid" on Wednesday and Thursday and that his prospects for playing were "very encouraging." Smith injured his ankle in the third quarter of last Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills . He underwent X-rays at the stadium and an MRI exam Monday, which showed no significant injury, a source said. He was seen walking with a limp Wednesday, but Smith stated matter-of-factly that he intended to play. The spiraling Jets (2-8) have lost five in a row. Some media members and fans are calling for rookie Cade Klubnik , who replaced Smith last Sunday, but Glenn has made it clear that Smith is the undisputed starter. Glenn said that Smith is performing well and that it would be "disrespectful" to replace him for the sake of evaluating Klubnik, a fourth-round pick from Clemson. The Jets hope Smith can lead the offense out of its funk -- nine straight quarters without a touchdown. They will be without their No. 3 and No. 4 receivers: rookie Omar Cooper Jr (ankle, hip) and Isaiah Williams (ribs). Tim Patrick , a healthy scratch last week, could be in the No. 3 role against the Chargers. They also could elevate veteran Sterling Shepard from the practice squad.

stories.title: Drake Maye ankle injury: Is the Patriots' season over? Can Tommy DeVito step up?
stories.summary: If the QB doesn't return in 2026, New England faces an uphill battle against some of the NFL's best teams.
stories.detailText: The outlook for the New England Patriots ' 2026 season has been dramatically altered. After suffering an injury on the Patriots' first drive against the Detroit Lions on Sunday, quarterback Drake Maye did not fly back from Munich with the team out of caution. Sources have told ESPN, Maye fractured his right fibula -- an injury that won't require surgery but is expected to sideline him deep into the regular season, if he is able to return this year at all. The 5-5 Patriots haven't been among the AFC's elite in 2026, but were hoping to make a charge to the playoffs -- and Maye potentially finding his past runner-up MVP form was one of their silver linings. When Maye was taking care of the football and extending plays, the Patriots were explosive and flashed potential to hang with the best -- as a Week 4 win at the Buffalo Bills showed. But when Maye was not buttoned-up with his decision-making (he entered Sunday with 11 INTs) the Patriots struggled. When he was cleaner in that area, it was just enough to get by some of the league's lower-echelon teams, with close wins against the New York Jets and Miami Dolphins , who have won a combined three games this season. Coach Mike Vrabel often says it's hard to win when a team's best players don't play well, and simply put, Maye is the team's best offensive player. Entering Week 10, he ranked top five in the NFL in Total QBR (74.2), passing touchdowns (18), yards per attempt (8.4), rushing yards by a quarterback (219) and rushing touchdowns by a quarterback (3). Now potentially without Maye for weeks or even the season, the question is can the team make it back to the playoffs? ESPN Patriots reporter Mike Reiss answers some of the top questions about the trickle-down effect of Maye's injury and analyst Matt Bowen answers a fantasy question on what to expect if you have Patriots players in your lineup. Is the Patriots' 2026 season over? When Vrabel was hired as head coach in January 2025, he said the team's goals were to win the division, host home playoff games and compete for championships. Their odds of doing that without Maye are closer to zero, starting with the current standings -- they are 5-5 while the AFC East rival Bills are 8-1. Here is the rest of the Patriots' schedule: they are on the bye in Week 11 before a road trip to face the winless Los Angeles Chargers , then two huge home games in a span of five days -- vs. the Bills (Dec. 6) and the Minnesota Vikings (Dec. 10). Then they're at the Kansas City Chiefs and the New York Jets before finishing the year with home games against the Denver Broncos and the Miami Dolphins . They have played poorly the past two weeks in blowout losses to the Packers and Lions, ravaged by injuries across the roster, but Maye's presence -- even as he battled through inconsistent play with turnovers -- gave them a sliver of hope. Consider what happened Sunday: After New England's opening drive when Maye was injured on the final play, the Patriots totaled seven points and gained 82 yards over 10 drives, averaging 1.9 yards per play (not including kneel down). New England punted on eight of those drives, with seven three-and-outs. Maye has been the driving force behind the passing game. Entering Sunday, Patriots pass catchers recorded 38.1% of their yards after the catch, the third-lowest total in the NFL behind the Texans (37.1%) and Giants (36.8%), per ESPN Research. The defense has also mightily struggled as of late, giving the offense little room for error. Since Week 7, the Patriots are giving up the second-most yards per game (411.5), behind only the 1-8 Tennessee Titans . With some of the NFL's elite teams on the horizon, life without Maye could look bleak. What is Drake Maye's possible recovery timeline? Maye suffered no additional ligament damage, sources told ESPN, which leaves open the possibility, but hardly a certainty, that Maye could return toward the end of the season if New England is in playoff contention. The recovery timeline for fractured ankles has varied, depending on the severity. In January, Broncos QB Bo Nix suffered a broken ankle and underwent surgery two days later. The initial recovery timetable reported was 12 weeks . In April, he underwent a clean-up surgery to fix bone spurs. Nix, who had a history of ankle injuries, was ready for training camp in July. In September 2022, 49ers QB Trey Lance underwent surgery on his right ankle after suffering "a fibula fracture and ligament disruption" in a game. The injury ended his season and required a follow-up surgery in December of that year to remove hardware that was causing irritation. He was cleared to participate in OTAs the following April. In 2024, 49ers linebacker Fred Warner said he had been playing most of the season with a fractured bone in his ankle . What can the offense get out of Tommy DeVito ? Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels has been through this before, most recently in 2016 when Tom Brady was serving a four-game NFL suspension and Jimmy Garoppolo and Jacoby Brissett stepped in to help the team to a 3-1 record. McDaniels' offense has flexibility to play to the specific strengths of the quarterback, with an obvious example coming with some designed runs for Brissett in 2016 that never would have been called with Brady. DeVito struggled Sunday when taking over for Maye, and Vrabel noted it was a tough position for him to be thrust into because backups don't receive many, if any, first-team repetitions during the week of practice. "There were some things that he missed, but also not having a ton of live action since training camp, and really, I think he'll be ready to go coming out of the bye," Vrabel said. "I think that he'll be able to look at some things and understand, whether that's being able to transfer up into the pocket, get us in the right play, get the ball out quicker or look at protections or rotation, whatever that may be. I think that'll all improve." DeVito had success with the deep ball in the preseason, and made improvements processing information on defensive coverages, so some of the things he has going for him are similar to Maye. And, of course, DeVito briefly caught fire with the New York Giants when thrust into a similar situation. In eight career starts (all with the Giants), DeVito is 3-5 with a 26.4 QBR, 65.3% completion rate, 1,170 passing yards for seven touchdowns, one interception and 34 sacks. He isn't as mobile as Maye, with only 36 rushes for 198 yards during those starts. Vrabel reflected optimism in the backup QB they signed to a two-year contract with a maximum value of $7.4 million in March. "I have a lot of confidence in Tommy," Vrabel said Monday. "I know his toughness is going to be through the charts, and his competitiveness will be exactly what we need." Could the Patriots explore other options at quarterback? That is a longer-shot scenario in terms of signing someone to be the starter, mainly due to the intricacies of the offense and the time crunch -- and also because there aren't many, if any, capable starters available. A more likely option initially is to utilize the 17-player practice squad to add a third layer of quarterback depth behind DeVito and rookie Behren Morton , the seventh-round pick from Texas Tech. Another avenue to explore would be other teams' practice squads to see if there is a worthy option to sign to the 53-man roster in a backup role. There are 15 quarterbacks on practice squads, a group including Will Levis (Jets), Nick Mullens (Jaguars), Kyle Trask (Cowboys) Hendon Hooker (Titans), Jake Browning (Chargers) and Luke Altmyer (Lions). "I don't see that being the case right now, but we'll have conversations and we'll discuss it and we'll look and see," Vrabel said Monday about the possibility of adding a quarterback. On Friday, the Indianapolis Colts released QB Daniel Jones , who could also be an option for the Patriots to explore. How have injuries decimated the Patriots this season? New England mostly had good fortune health-wise in its surprise run to the Super Bowl last year, and 2026 has been the other side of the coin. Vrabel noted in a Monday radio interview that it evens out over time. It began in the spring when tight end Julian Hill , who they signed to be their No. 2 option and a blocking force, sustained a season-ending knee injury and veteran outside linebacker Harold Landry III had an undisclosed injury that landed him on the physically unable to perform list (where he remains). Then receiver A.J. Brown suffered a right high-ankle sprain in the season opener and hasn't looked the same since a strong training camp. They placed both starting guards on injured reserve, along with No. 2 receiver Romeo Doubs (shoulder) and No. 2 running back TreVeyon Henderson (illness), among others. And now possibly Maye. Teams are allowed eight designations to return from IR and the Patriots have already used five of them and will likely max out all eight by season's end. "We just have to find some consistency, hopefully, in the lineup with the guys that are coming in and out and everything else, guys that we've built up through the draft and the guys that know one system. But that sometimes always isn't going to be the case, and that's where we're at now," Vrabel said. What should fantasy managers do with the Patriots' offense in fantasy football? This injury will have a major impact on the Patriots' roster from a fantasy perspective . DeVito can provide some upside as a runner, but he should only be played in deeper Superflex formats as a QB2. WR A.J. Brown left Sunday's game with a hamstring injury, and he has played in only four games this season due to multiple injuries. When he returns, however, Brown's value declines, fitting in lineups as a WR3. DeMario Douglas now becomes a matchup-dependent WR3, while Mack Hollins is a bye week fill-in for deeper leagues. TE Hunter Henry was a top target for Maye, but I am anticipating a reduced amount of red zone work here, which moves him down to the TE1/TE2 line. In the backfield with TreVeyon Henderson on IR (illness), Rhamondre Stevenson could see a bump in volume if the Patriots are more run-heavy, plus he can operate as an outlet/checkdown option for DeVito in the pass game, which keeps him in the RB2 range. -- Matt Bowen

stories.title: Jimmy Garoppolo’s reunion may not be with the Rams
stories.summary: The Rams should still consider him as a backup option for the home stretch.
stories.detailText: If the Los Angeles Rams lost Matthew Stafford for any amount of time this season, would you trust the current backup quarterback options? Would you feel any better if an experienced veteran, like Jimmy Garoppolo, could step in? There’s nothing to indicate Stafford is at any increased risk of an injury or missing snaps for any reason. But as the NFL playoffs approach and the margin for error shrinks closer to zero, it’s hard not to think about protecting yourself against calamity. That’s especially true for a Rams team that has dealt with tons of injuries this year, including another serious one to a starting offensive lineman just this week. This is relevant now because Garoppolo, who spent the 2024 and 2025 seasons in Los Angeles, is suddenly being linked to other playoff contenders , like another one of his former teams, the New England Patriots. After initial reporting on the matter by Jordan Schultz, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler discussed the situation this week and threw some cold water on the topic but stopped short of completely killing the idea. Specifically, he mentioned that there are questions about whether or not the 12-year veteran has any actual desire to play again. The #Patriots are expected to explore the QB market during the bye week, from free agents such as Jimmy Garoppolo, who has previously played for OC Josh McDaniels, to potentially adding a QB off another team’s practice squad. Tommy DeVito is currently expected to become the… pic.twitter.com/2DLcMGnvKl — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) November 16, 2026 He also mentioned, however, that Garoppolo enjoyed playing on the west coast. That could work in the Rams’ favor, obviously. Don’t get it twisted, this is not an earth-shattering kind of hypothetical personnel scenario. This is a quarterback who had good moments in several years as a starter, but isn’t exactly a Hall of Fame candidate. He would purely be an insurance policy if Los Angeles wanted to pursue that route. And realistically, if Stafford missed more than a game or a couple games at the absolute most, things would get dire in a hurry for the Rams. Still, the alternatives currently are Stetson Bennett, who’s taken a whopping 10 offensive snaps over four seasons (all of which have come this year) and Ty Simpson, the first-round pick who still hasn’t seen the field and who is a known project player. Rams week-by-week list of major injuries through 9 weeks: pic.twitter.com/fwBEtvo4aD — Erin Coscarelli (@erincoscarelli) November 9, 2026 This idea isn’t completely out of left field, either, as it was discussed over the offseason as the backup job was still in flux in the wake of the Simpson pick in the NFL draft. There isn’t much that’s controversial about re-signing a generally inoffensive backup quarterback. The Rams have enough personnel concerns that they likely don’t have to go full bore after another reserve quarterback right now. But if push came to shove and they had to sign one out of desperation, Garoppolo still makes sense. That’s the situation the Patriots are quite literally in right now with Drake Maye injured. It would be a terrible scenario regardless, but a slightly less devastating one with a more reliable backup in the fray.

stories.title: Colts officially place Daniel Jones on waivers
stories.summary: Daniel Jones is officially on the waiver wire.
stories.detailText: Daniel Jones is officially on the waiver wire. The NFL transaction report has gone out this afternoon, and Jones appears as a waiver from the Colts. After the trade deadline, every player who gets released by his team has to go on waivers before he becomes a free agent. That means any team that wants Jones on his current contract can claim him, but that is extraordinarily unlikely to happen. As the waiver transaction notes, Jones is a vested veteran with a fully guaranteed salary for the rest of this season. No team is going to want to claim that salary. Once he clears waivers, however, he'll be an unrestricted free agent, free to sign with any team, and it won't be surprising if some team wants to add him for veteran depth. Jones has been terrible this season, but he's been a competent starter at times in his career, and a team that wants an experienced backup may be interested in signing him for a minimal salary. Jones was also waived almost exactly two years ago, on November 22, 2024. He cleared waivers and signed with the Vikings' practice squad before signing with the Colts after that season.

stories.title: Saints at Bears Q&A: Dennis Allen Revenge Game Part 2
stories.summary: The Chicago Bears face the New Orleans Saints on Sunday. To get you set for this matchup, we sat down with Canal Street Chronicles (SB Nation’s Saints site) for a Q&A.
stories.detailText: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 18: Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen of the Chicago Bears looks on during the fourth quarter against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Bears are back from their bye week and ready to welcome the New Orleans Saints to Soldier Field. The Bears are sitting at 7-2 and in prime position to make the playoffs. The Saints sit at 3-6, but fortunately for them, they are only a game and a half out of first in the weak NFC South. To help get you set for this matchup, we sat down with Nic Jennings of our sister site, Canal Street Chronicles (SB Nation’s New Orleans Saints site), to get you set for their opponent. 1. The Saints are sitting at 3-6, but from my outsider view, I feel like this team is close to clicking, potentially even the back half of this season and start winning some football games. What’s the vibe around the Saints for the fan base? The vibe around the fanbase isn’t great right now. I don’t think fans have given up on the players, but rather they’ve given up on Kellen Moore, Mickey Loomis, and Gayle Benson. The Saints are somehow only one game out of first place in the division, so there’s still hope that they can turn things around and make a push. But it is frustrating to watch a roster with this much talent continue to fail to put everything together. At this point, I think changes need to be made within the regime, and until that happens, I expect the vibes around the fanbase to remain largely the same, win or lose. 2. I’ll be honest, when Kellen Moore was hired, I didn’t think much of him as a head coaching candidate, but I’ve come around on him a little. What did Saints fans think of the hire last year, ar and where are they at with him midway through 2026? The initial reaction to Moore’s hiring was that the Saints finally had another offensive-minded head coach in the building who could bring a refreshing change to the way things had been done. However, that optimism has long since faded. Moore is running out of excuses, and quite frankly, I don’t think there is any way he can win the fanbase back at this point. Through his first 26 games, the Saints have trailed in every single one of those games, while failing to score in the first quarter 18 times. Two consistent issues have plagued Moore’s teams across both seasons: slow starts that force the Saints to claw their way back into games and an offense that continues to look dysfunctional, with a putrid run game forcing Tyler Shough to carry the team on his back. At this point, the frustration has gone beyond results, and fans are rightfully questioning whether Moore is the guy to lead this team moving forward. 3. I’ve never been a fan of how Mickey Loomis has handled the cap and the rebuild/reload (whatever you want to call it) of this roster. Are Saints fans still behind Loomis or do they want to see a change? Yes, the fanbase still wants a change in the front office, but it’s not necessarily because of the financial side of things. The Saints are expected to finally be out of “cap hell” next season and back to operating with more financial flexibility. However, Mickey Loomis’ draft-day decisions and head coaching hires since Sean Payton’s departure have taken their toll on the fanbase. For a team that has been in a rebuilding phase, it’s difficult to get out of that cycle without consistently drafting impactful players, and that’s been one of the biggest issues. The tricky part is that Loomis is the NFL’s longest-tenured general manager at 25 years and has won a Super Bowl with the franchise. Given his history and relationship with the organization, I don’t see Gayle Benson moving on from him unless he decides to step down himself. That’s what makes the situation so complicated. 4. Tyler Shough certainly looks like he’s taking strides this year, but he’s also 27 years old. Do you think Shough is a legit NFL QB that can lead this Saints offense for the next 5 to 7 years? Absolutely. Shough is the real deal, and his teammates rally behind him. He’s been one of the few consistent bright spots for the Saints this season, along with Chris Olave, Chase Young, and Carl Granderson. Shough showed a lot of promise in his limited starts as a rookie, then attacked the offseason and blew expectations out of the water. He’s carried that same momentum into this season. His ball placement, ability to stretch the field with his arm, poise in the pocket, and ability to extend plays with his legs give the Saints a dimension offensively that they haven’t really had. And most importantly, he has that clutch gene. He’s shown he can make plays when the Saints need them most. I do think there are still things he can improve on, and he’s had a bit of a rough stretch over the last two weeks. Like I previously mentioned, the offense has developed a habit of starting slowly, and while I’d put more of that on Kellen Moore, Shough still plays a role in getting the offense into a rhythm. Though,gh to Shough’s credit, the Saints have a nonexistent rushing attack, which hasn’t eased the pressure on Shough and the passing game one bit. But overall, I’ve seen more than enough to believe he can be the long-term answer in New Orleans. As for his age, to put things into perspective, Drew Brees joined the Saints at 27 years old, and it felt like he was in New Orleans for a lifetime. Even as a 26-year-old rookie, Shough was visibly more prepared than his fellow rookies. I view his age as a benefit rather than a drawback and believe he has a long career ahead of him. 5. What is one player on the Saints offense and one player on the Saints defense that may not be a headliner that you think can make an impact on Sunday? Do you have a prediction for the game? On offense, I’ll go with Devaughn Vele. After the Saints invested a fourth-round pick in him last year to pry him away from Denver, Vele has come in and become the contested-catch slot receiver the Saints have been searching for since Michael Thomas. He’s quickly become one of Tyler Shough’s favorite targets and has established himself as the go-to guy in third-and-long situations. With Jordyn Tyson back in the mix alongside Chris Olave, Vele’s production has dwindled a bit over the past two games. That said, I believe his opportunities will come, and he’s proven he can take advantage of them. For a six-foot-five receiver to move the way he does and possess that type of body control is truly remarkable. On defense, keep an eye on second-year defensive back, Jonas Sanker. He consistently finds his way to the football and has been impressive in his first year starting in the slot. He returned a fumble for a touchdown against the Vikings and had another return for a touchdown in Week 1 against the Lions that was called back after Jared Goff apparently “intended” to throw the football forward. With Justin Reid now out of the picture in New Orleans, perhaps we see Sanker move back to his natural position at safety, where he spent his rookie season.

teamStories.detailText: If the Raiders wanted to ease Fernando Mendoza into his new job, they have a peculiar way of showing it. First came the Seahawks, who turned his starting debut into a chess match with consequences. Six times, those consequences involved Mendoza being dropped to the ground with the ball still in his hands. Next up are the Broncos, rested from their bye and waiting in Denver. After that, the Browns in Cleveland. It is difficult to imagine a much more treacherous introduction to professional quarterbacking. Three defenses capable of making experienced quarterbacks uncomfortable, with the last two getting the rookie in their own buildings. Fernando Mendoza #15 and Cody White #82 of the Las Vegas Raiders warm up at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. The Seahawks won 21-13. Getty Images The schedule will eventually offer something more forgiving. For now, Mendoza is getting an education that requires an ice bath afterward. And somewhere down the road, he might appreciate it. The disguised coverages, the pressure arriving from unexpected places, the difference between what a defense shows before the snap and what it becomes afterward. Every uncomfortable experience gives him something to recognize the next time he sees it. But there is another education taking place, and the Raiders need to pay just as much attention to it. John Spytek, Tom Brady and Klint Kubiak are learning what they have to put around their young quarterback. That makes Sunday’s game against Denver, and the six remaining afterward, an evaluation of everyone involved in making this work. Mendoza has responsibilities. He has to process information faster, understand when to abandon a play and get the ball out before a manageable situation becomes a drive-killing sack. He accepted those responsibilities after the Seattle game. Good for him. The entire building needs to do the same. The Raiders rushed for 65 yards on 24 attempts against the Seahawks. Brock Bowers hurt his ankle on the opening series, and an offense already short on dependable answers had even fewer. Las Vegas Raiders General Manager John Spytek arrives at Allegiant Stadium for a game against the Seattle Seahawks in Las Vegas on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images Those are organizational problems with consequences for the quarterback. Start with the interior offensive line. Mendoza needs room to step into throws and a running game that makes second down feel like an opportunity. The Raiders have to determine which players can provide that consistently and where upgrades are necessary. Every failed block deserves examination, including whether the problem was talent, technique or communication. Those distinctions will matter when Spytek starts deciding how to spend another offseason. Then there is the receiver the Raiders still need. A premier talent alongside Bowers would change how defenses prepare for Las Vegas. Give Mendoza someone who threatens downfield, commands attention and wins when the coverage is good, and the entire offense benefits. Bowers gets more favorable opportunities. The running game faces different defensive decisions. Mendoza gets a receiver he can trust when the play requires someone to make something happen. The Raiders need that kind of two-headed problem for opponents. They also need to understand that supporting a quarterback extends to the possessions when he is standing on the sideline. A defense that cannot consistently stop the run gives the opposing offense control of the game. It keeps Mendoza waiting, limits his opportunities and increases the pressure to produce when he finally gets the ball back. The interior defensive line needs more star power and ruggedness. Someone has to disrupt the blocking, hold the point of attack and make an offense reconsider running directly at the Raiders. Maxx Crosby needs a reliable complementary pass rusher, too. The attention he commands should create opportunities that another defender regularly turns into sacks, hurried throws and stalled drives. The secondary has promising young players whose development deserves investment and patience. But young defensive backs also benefit when the quarterback has to throw on schedule and the defense can anticipate passing situations. Fox Sports broadcast analyst Tom Brady looks on before a game between the Dallas Cowboys and San Francisco 49ers in Arlington, Texas, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It all connects. Better run defense creates longer third downs. Better pressure helps coverage. More stops give the offense additional chances and a little breathing room. These next games will help reveal which pieces belong and which must be added. The Raiders selected Mendoza because they believe he can become a great quarterback. His first starts offer the beginnings of that picture, with every adjustment and mistake adding detail. They also expose the work required around him. Sunday is another opportunity for Mendoza to show what he learned. It is another opportunity for the Raiders to figure out what they must do about what they are learning.

teamStories.title: 3 causes for concern for Raiders Week 11 vs Broncos
Las Vegas Raiders-Denver Broncos FEED Topic: Kolton Miller, DJ Glaze vs. Nik Bonitto, Jonathon Cooper
teamStories.summary: Facing one of the NFL’s best edge-rush duos, the Raiders’ OTs will must be on point to protect Fernando Mendoza.
teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks managed to get six sacks on Fernando Mendoza in his starting debut last week , and pressure on the quarterback will be another major key to the game for the Las Vegas Raiders’ offense in Week 11. The Denver Broncos present the same problem but in a different way than Seattle, one that will place a greater emphasis on the Raiders’ offensive line, especially tackles Kolton Miller and DJ Glaze . Led by head coach Mike Macdonald, the Seahawks defense uses a creative scheme to help manufacture pressure and create confusion for opposing quarterbacks. To a certain extent, they’re able to work around or neutralize the offensive line by attacking running backs in pass protection or forcing quarterbacks to account for free rushers by throwing hot. Last week was a perfect example, as top cornerback Devon Witherspoon led the team with two of the six sacks. Meanwhile, Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph isn’t afraid to blitz, but that’s to help create one-on-one opportunities for their defensive linemen, especially edge rushers Nik Bonitto and Jonathon Cooper. Bonitto is coming off back-to-back Pro Bowl seasons, where he registered 27.5 sacks and 133 pressures, per Pro Football Focus , in 2024 and 2025 combined. This season, he’s recorded 4.5 sacks in nine games and ranks tied for 19th among edges with 30 pressures . Meanwhile, Cooper notched 18.5 sacks and 112 pressures in the two previous seasons to give the Broncos a quality No. 2 pass-rusher on the edge. In 2026, he’s only participated in three games due to off-field issues in the offseason and has just 10 pressures and 0.5 sacks on 77 pass-rush snaps. So, Cooper’s numbers are down as a consequence of his actions, but his track record on the field speaks for itself. On the other side of the trenches, Miller has an impressive resume in pass protection but has been regressing this year. With 32 pressures on 379 opportunities, per PFF , his 8.4 percent pressure rate is the highest it’s been since the 2018 first-round pick’s rookie year (11.0 percent). But Glaze is trending in the opposite direction, going from 8.3 percent and 8.0 percent pressure rates in his first two seasons, respectively, to 4.0 percent ( 15 pressures on 379 opportunities ) this year. With the Raiders shifting from Kirk Cousins to Mendoza last week and seeing their playoff hopes rapidly decline over the last roughly two months, we’ve reached the point in the season where it’s time to start looking at building for the future. Part of that is making sure the rookie quarterback can stay upright enough to make some plays and build confidence heading into next year. The other part is evaluating the team’s needs before the offseason gets going. It would be remiss to talk about the Broncos’ pass rush and not mention Zach Allen, who currently leads all defensive tackles with 38 pressures and has 4.5 sacks . However, it feels like a foregone conclusion that Las Vegas will have to address its guard situation this spring. Meanwhile, offensive tackle is still up in the air, and this weekend will be a good litmus test for Miller and Glaze. Is the veteran left tackle past his prime, where it’s time to find a new blind side protector? Is the third-year pro’s growth legitimate? How they fare against one of the NFL’s best edge-rush duos over the last few years, Bonitto and Cooper, on Sunday will go a long way toward answering those questions. So, for this week’s game day discussion on The FEED , we’ll be keeping tabs on how well Miller and Glaze can protect the edges to keep Mendoza clean in Denver. The game kicks off at 1:25 p.m. PST and will air on CBS (check your local listings). I look forward to talkin’ some ball with y’all!

teamStories.summary: Denver defense ranked 9th in points allowed this season but susceptible to air and ground attacks
teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images With just 186 total points allowed in nine games, the Denver Broncos boast the ninth-best defensive unit in that regard, which will make it tough sledding for the Las Vegas Raiders this Sunday. The Silver & Black Express rolls into Mile High with a new conductor in prized rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza a road divisional matchup against the first-place Broncos (tied with the Kansas City Chiefs at 7-2 overall). The No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, Mendoza made his first career start against the stifling Seattle Seahawks defense and Las Vegas fell 21-13 in Week 10. Another formidable defense awaits Mendoza in Week 11 as Vance Joseph’s Denver squad comes off a bye week after a wire-to-wire Week 9 26-21 win at the Carolina Panthers two Sunday’s ago. To hear the 23-year-old budding franchise quarterback tell it, however, he wouldn’t have it any other way as he preps for his second-career NFL start this Sunday in Denver. “I believe getting thrown in the fire is the best way to learn, and the Seahawks and the Broncos both have considerably elite defenses,” Mendoza said when asked what it’s like getting thrown into the fire against two quality NFL defenses. “I really believe every NFL defense is elite because when you’re playing at this level, the margin for error is so small, and all the defensive coordinators are geniuses. “So, I’m honored and blessed to go against a great defensive coordinator in Coach Robbie (Raiders defensive coordinator Rob Leonard) every single day, especially in OTAs and fall camp and training camp. So, I believe that’s helped prepare me, an now I’m excited to embark on this journey with my teammates.” #Broncos ’ Bo Nix on peaking at the right time and how different the QB experience is when making 44th start compared to second like #Raiders ’ Fernando Mendoza pic.twitter.com/kvgaDzKQ2y — Troy Renck (@TroyRenck) November 18, 2026 How Mendoza settles during his second start against an aggressive Broncos defense bears watching. The Seahawks produced a blueprint of how to and how not to defend the Indiana product last week. When protected with a clean (and sometimes noisy) pocket, Mendoza was a smooth operator going through progressions and using his accurate and strong arm to deliver the football to Raiders pass catchers. In the first half, Mendoza went 11-of-13 for 90 yards including his first-career touchdown run. When Seattle saw enough of that, head coach and defensive play caller Mike Macdonald went to his bag of tricks of blitz, simulated pressure, and exotic alignments to take advantage of the neophyte signal caller and Mendoza went 6-of-16 for 53 yards in the second half while absorbing six sacks and 12 hits. Expect Joseph to stick to a similar script and bring the pain on the 6-foot-5 and 225-pound Raiders quarterback. Especially considering the Broncos have 84 quarterback hits on the season alongside 26 sacks. Zach Allen is an ultra-productive defensive lineman who plays both inside as a tackle and outside as an edge rusher and paces Denver with 4.5 sacks and 23 quarterback hits. Edge rusher Nik Bonitto is right there with him with 4.5 sacks and 11 QB hits while defensive tackle Malcolm Roach is disruptive with four sacks and 13 quarterback hits. Heat-seeking inside linebacker Alex Singleton is a quality clean-up man and is tied for the league lead in tackles at 107 (Raiders inside linebacker Nakobe Dean is who he is tied with) and also has two sacks and six quarterback hits on his stat sheet. All of this is presented to note Mendoza’s accurate arm and fresh legs are integral to Las Vegas’ aspirations to walk out of Denver with an AFC West win. That dual-threat ability is essential to counter the Joseph’s defense that is every bit as creative and chaotic as Macdonald’s group. All it takes is a few successful scrambles to make a defense bite — Seattle did this — and with Mendoza lauded for his cerebral ways and ability to not make the same mistake again, watching the film from last Sunday’s loss will showcase just that. The second-quarter 22-yard dart Mendoza zipped to wide receiver Cody White is an example of this. Mendoza felt pressure, began to scramble but kept his eyes downfield, and his ability to thrown on the arm and velocity on the fast ball were on full display. Fernando Mendoza ➡️ Cody White for the first down! SEAvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/KmbkHKSAKr — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 “We have a great strength and conditioning staff here, and performance staff as a whole, whether it’s the training staff, nutrition, strength. There’s so many different aspects of it, so I’m blessed to be a part of it,” Mendoza began when as he answered a question about his mobility being an underrated aspect of his game, “I believe I’ve gotten faster since being here, and I’m grateful for that because in the NFL, those players are fast.” Those fleet feet will come in handy to escape the exotic blitzes Joseph is expected to deploy. Especially with Las Vegas ground game grinding to a halt consistently over the course of the 2026 season, much to the chagrin of Raiders rookie head coach and offensive play caller Klint Kubiak. Mendoza’s ability to run helps provide an alternative run game and scrambling for hidden yards and first downs can frustrate the opposing defense. Kubiak should again go play-action heavy with designed rollouts and bootlegs to vary the launch point of the ball and give his talented rookie cleaner passing lane and run-pass options. Mendoza has the arm talent to push the ball downfield and by getting the ball into the hands of his pass catchers quickly or downfield, Las Vegas can take advantage of Denver’s penchant to whiff on tackles as the team has a high 16.2 percent missed tackle rate. Of course, it’d help to have a healthy Brock Bowers available as the tight end is the Raiders’ de facto WR1. Mendoza is keen on balancing staying in the pocket and winning with this arm while also knowing when to run and gain positive yards against Denver. “There were a lot of moments in the game that we reviewed after in the film, whether it’s Coach Kubiak, Coach (Andrew) Janocko or Coach (Mike) Sullivan, they made comments on whatever the situation was, whether it was some inefficiency or a play that in the future we want to change. So, I’m taking those day by day and trying to improve on them,” Mendoza said regarding staying in the pocket longer to deliver a throw instead of taking off as quickly as he did in his first start. Listen to what the support from Raider Nation means to Fernando Mendoza (Via CBS, @mickakers ) pic.twitter.com/esG3mYtH5F — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) November 16, 2026 While the Broncos boast the ninth-best red zone defense — teams have visited the space between the 20-yard line and end zone 29 times for only 15 touchdowns for a 51.7 percent conversion rate — they are susceptible to getting yards piled upon them allowing 3,195 yards for 27th most amongst the 32 teams. That right there is a textbook example of a bend-but-not-break defense. Head-to-Head Sunday’s Mile High tilt marks the 134th time the Raiders and Broncos go toe-to-toe. The Silver & Black lead the all-time series 73-58-2 (72-5702 in regular season play, 1-1 in the playoffs) but are riding a four-game losing skid against the Horsemen. The last time Las Vegas beat Denver was in January of 2024, a 27-14 victory inside Allegiant Stadium. Since that tilt, the Broncos have won the next four meetings 34-18, 29-19, 10-7, and 24-17. The pair of longtime AFC West foes will meet again in Week 15 in Las Vegas. Quotes of Note “We were in a zone, it was an extended play, and expecting a quick throw and it became something — when extended plays happen, we always talk about the second play, and plaster, and those types of things. Anytime something doesn’t go well I wish I would have called something different.” —Las Vegas Raiders defensive coordinator Rob Leonard on Seattle Seahawks wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s 71-yard touchdown on a broken play “I think with Brock (Bowers) and anyone in the tight end, wide receiver, anyone, they’re constantly talking and as they grow and mesh together it’s something that will continue to benefit us as an offense.” —Las Vegas Raiders offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko on the chemistry between pass catchers and quarterback Fernando Mendoza

teamStories.detailText: HENDERSON, Nev. -- Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) is questionable for Sunday's divisional matchup against the Denver Broncos , coach Klint Kubiak said Friday. Bowers practiced for two straight days after not participating Wednesday and said he's "feeling all right." Kubiak didn't say whether Bowers will work out pregame to determine his game status. When Bowers was asked if he felt optimistic about his availability for the Week 11 contest with playoff implications, he said: "We'll see." "I don't know. We still have some conversations to have," Bowers added. Bowers injured his right ankle on the opening drive of the Raiders' 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks . At the 11:31 mark, left tackle Kolton Miller and a Seahawks defender tumbled over Bowers' leg during an Ashton Jeanty rushing attempt. Bowers remained on the ground before walking off the field under his own power. Bowers went into the medical tent and then returned to the field for Fernando Mendoza 's 10-yard touchdown run. Bowers headed to the locker room after that play and was listed as questionable to return by the team. He returned with 13:30 to go in the second quarter and made a 12-yard reception on third down. Later in the quarter, Bowers went back to the locker room, where he stayed for the rest of the first half before ultimately being ruled out. Bowers finished with two catches for 18 yards, upping his season totals to 50 catches for 676 yards and six touchdowns. The Raiders' offense collapsed in his absence, totaling just 27 net yards in the second half. "I really wanted to play, so I was just doing everything I could to get back out there, like just trying a new tape job and stuff," Bowers said while reflecting on last week's game. "Felt it each time I went back out there. It was tough." The Raiders also face a kicker dilemma. Matt Gay (hip) is questionable to play. Gay didn't practice Thursday but was on the field Wednesday and Friday, and Kubiak said he practiced well. With uncertainty surrounding Gay's injury, the Raiders worked out three kickers Thursday: Lucas Havrisik , Younghoe Koo and John Parker Romo . If needed, the Raiders could elevate practice squad kicker and undrafted rookie Kansei Matsuzawa . "We have Plan B and a Plan C. We got Special K [Matsuzawa]," Kubiak said.
